     its destination. The protocol delivers into NEST 96 Well Plate 200 µL Flat (slot 3,
     load name nest_96_wellplate_200ul_flat), which is a flat plate. A thermocycler block is
     drilled for thin-walled 0.2 ml PCR wells; a flat plate does not fit in it, so the
     reaction can never be run. The plate map checks what each well holds, not what plate it
     is.

   Fix: Load nest_96_wellplate_100ul_pcr_full_skirt (or the 200 ul PCR plate, or PCR strips
     on the aluminium block) as the destination; a flat plate cannot go in a thermocycler.

labware.title: The wrong kind of plate: NEST 96 Well Plate 200 µL Flat is a flat plate, and PCR setup needs a PCR plate or PCR strips
labware.explanation: The plate map says the technique is PCR setup, which needs a PCR plate or PCR strips as its destination. The protocol delivers into NEST 96 Well Plate 200 µL Flat (slot 3, load name nest_96_wellplate_200ul_flat), which is a flat plate. A thermocycler block is drilled for thin-walled 0.2 ml PCR wells; a flat plate does not fit in it, so the reaction can never be run. The plate map checks what each well holds, not what plate it is.
labware.fix: Load nest_96_wellplate_100ul_pcr_full_skirt (or the 200 ul PCR plate, or PCR strips on the aluminium block) as the destination; a flat plate cannot go in a thermocycler.

protocol.py: 6 biology problems (1 error, 3 warnings, 2 notes).

1. ERROR SOURCE-TOO-SHALLOW: The pipette draws air from well A1 in slot 5: the liquid is
below the tip
   line 124:  p300.aspirate(23, reservoir["A1"])
   At line 124 the p300_single_gen2 draws 23 ul from well A1 in slot 5 with its tip 1 mm
   above the bottom of the well. By then the well holds 184 ul, which in this NEST 12 Well
   Reservoir 15 mL reaches only 0.87 mm up: the tip is above the liquid and draws air (this
   line did it 8 times, after 40 times in the liquid; 184 ul of air in all). The simulator
   does not notice: it does not follow the liquid. The 8 wells filled from these draws got
   air instead of liquid.
   Affected: well A1 in slot 5.
   Also reached 8 other wells: wells D5, D6, D7, D8, D9, D10, D11 and D12 in slot 3.
   Fix: Keep the liquid above the tip. This well needs about 258 ul in it for the surface to
   reach 1 mm. Load that much more than the run draws; or draw from a smaller vessel (a tube
   lifts the liquid); or aspirate lower with `well.bottom(0.5)`.
   Source: Opentrons: liquid control (aspirates 1 mm above the bottom of the well by
   default)
           https://docs.opentrons.com/v2/basic_commands/liquids.html
   Source: Artel: automated liquid handlers as sources of error
           https://www.bioprocessintl.com/assays/automated-liquid-handlers-as-sources-of-error
   Source: Gilson guide to pipetting (immersion depth 2 to 3 mm for 1 to 100 ul)
           https://solutions.pipette.com/wp-content/uploads/Gilson-Guide-to-Pipetting.pdf
   Source: labautomation.io 7592: negative controls positive after aspirating air
           https://labautomation.io/t/aspiration-dispense-liquid-class-incompatibity/7592
   Source: Integra: 260 ul dead volume in a standard reservoir
           https://www.integra-biosciences.com/global/en/applications/minimizing-dead-volume-during-qpcr-set-divided-reservoir-assist-plus-pipetting-robot
   [b1bd3600001e]

2. WARNING COLD-MODULE-NEVER-SET: A temperature module was loaded but never set
   line 60:  p300.aspirate(240, component_block["A1"])
   At line 60 the robot draws from wells A1, A2, A3, A4, A5 and A6 in slot 4, on a
   temperature module that the protocol never sets. A temperature module stays at room
   temperature until `set_temperature` is called, so buffer (carrier), dntp (reagent), fwd
   primer (reagent), polymerase (reagent) and 2 more sat on a block that was never cold; the
   robot pipetted there 8 times over the run. The person setting up the deck sees a module
   and assumes it is cold. Wells: wells A1, A2, A3, A4, A5 and A6 in slot 4.
   Affected: wells A1, A2, A3, A4, A5 and A6 in slot 4.
   Fix: Call `temp_module.set_temperature(4)` before the first transfer from Opentrons 24
   Well Aluminum Block with NEST 1.5 mL Snapcap in slot 4, and `temp_module.deactivate()` at
   the end.
   Source: Opentrons, temperature module: at room temperature until set_temperature, which
   blocks
           https://docs.opentrons.com/v2/modules/temperature_module.html

The Opentrons simulator (8.8.2) passed this protocol with no error: it checks that the robot

findings.title: The pipette draws air from well A1 in slot 5: the liquid is below the tip
findings.explanation: At line 124 the p300_single_gen2 draws 23 ul from well A1 in slot 5 with its tip 1 mm above the bottom of the well. By then the well holds 184 ul, which in this NEST 12 Well Reservoir 15 mL reaches only 0.87 mm up: the tip is above the liquid and draws air (this line did it 8 times, after 40 times in the liquid; 184 ul of air in all). The simulator does not notice: it does not follow the liquid. The 8 wells filled from these draws got air instead of liquid.
findings.fix: Keep the liquid above the tip. This well needs about 258 ul in it for the surface to reach 1 mm. Load that much more than the run draws; or draw from a smaller vessel (a tube lifts the liquid); or aspirate lower with `well.bottom(0.5)`.

findings.title: A temperature module was loaded but never set
findings.explanation: At line 60 the robot draws from wells A1, A2, A3, A4, A5 and A6 in slot 4, on a temperature module that the protocol never sets. A temperature module stays at room temperature until `set_temperature` is called, so buffer (carrier), dntp (reagent), fwd primer (reagent), polymerase (reagent) and 2 more sat on a block that was never cold; the robot pipetted there 8 times over the run. The person setting up the deck sees a module and assumes it is cold. Wells: wells A1, A2, A3, A4, A5 and A6 in slot 4.
findings.fix: Call `temp_module.set_temperature(4)` before the first transfer from Opentrons 24 Well Aluminum Block with NEST 1.5 mL Snapcap in slot 4, and `temp_module.deactivate()` at the end.
